adaptive_models.name: DRDO habitable band, 17 plus or minus 3 C

source.citation: DRDO transfer of technology document, Solar Thermal Technology based System for Space Heating of Shelter in Cold Condition, DIHAR: the stored heat is used to maintain the comfortable habitable temperature (17 plus or minus 3 C) inside the shelter
source.note: A fixed band of 14 to 20 C that does not move with the outdoor temperature. It is DRDO's own number for a shelter in cold conditions, so Output 1 is judged against it first.

adaptive_models.name: India Model for Adaptive Comfort, naturally ventilated

source.citation: Manu, Shukla, Rawal, Thomas and de Dear, Field studies of thermal comfort across multiple climate zones for the subcontinent: India Model for Adaptive Comfort (IMAC), Building and Environment 98 (2016) 55-70, with the corrigendum in Building and Environment 106 (2016) 422-426
source.note: Neutral temperature 0.54 times the 30 day outdoor running mean plus 12.83 C, defined for a running mean of 12.5 to 31 C. The corrigendum revised Table 11 and Figures 2, 5 and 6, and the acceptability band half width has not been read off the corrected table, so this record stays pending. A Ladakh winter running mean sits far below 12.5 C, so outside summer this band is held at its floor and must not lead a result.

adaptive_models.name: India Model for Adaptive Comfort, residential, naturally ventilated

source.citation: Rawal and others, India Model for Adaptive Comfort residential, IMAC-R, 2022
source.note: Placeholder carrying the IMAC 2016 coefficients so the pipeline runs. The residential regression differs and MUST be substituted from the 2022 paper before this model is selected for a reported result.

fixed_targets.name: DRDO band lower edge through the night

source.citation: Lower edge of the DRDO habitable band of 17 plus or minus 3 C, held over the 18:00 to 06:00 window in which DIHAR's solar heated shelters were reported to be heated
source.note: The 14 C threshold is DRDO's; the 18:00 to 06:00 window is the operating window reported for the DIHAR system at Leh (Energetica India, 2025) and is the night the heating run and the night degree hours use.

fixed_targets.name: Eco-Niwas Samhita cold climate envelope check

source.citation: Eco-Niwas Samhita 2018, Bureau of Energy Efficiency, cold climate zone envelope requirements
source.note: Used as a secondary reference bound only. The envelope U-value limits it sets are checked separately in the buildability metrics.
